sections.h2: Where is Franklin, Massachusetts, and is it a town or a city?
sections.html:
Franklin sits in Norfolk County, southwest of Boston, along the Interstate 495 belt. It is officially the "Town of Franklin" but runs under a city form of government, one of thirteen Massachusetts municipalities that adopted a city structure and kept "Town of" in the name.

The 2020 census counted 33,261 people. The area totals about 27 square miles, almost all of it land. The elevation is around 299 feet, and the ZIP code is 02038. The town uses a council-manager structure, so a Town Administrator runs day-to-day operations rather than an elected mayor.

Franklin was first settled by Europeans in 1660 and was formed from the western part of Wrentham. It was incorporated on March 2, 1778, and it became the first municipality in the country named for Benjamin Franklin.

The town had hoped for a church bell from Franklin. He sent 116 books instead, and in 1790 the town decided to lend them to residents for free. That collection became the Franklin Public Library, which is described as the oldest running public library in the nation. The Ray Memorial Library building was dedicated in 1904.

Franklin is also the birthplace of Horace Mann, often called the father of American public education. The Red Brick School, built in 1833, kept operating until 2008. St. Mary's Catholic Church, with about 15,000 members, is the largest parish in the Boston Archdiocese.

sections.h2: What does the land look like, and why does it matter for a house?
sections.html:
Most of Franklin lies in the Charles River watershed, with a small southwestern corner draining to the Blackstone River. Principal streams include Mine, Shepard's, Miller, Uncas, Dix and Miscoe Brooks.

Much of the marshland along Mine Brook is protected by the Army Corps of Engineers Natural Valley Storage Project. The town also has the Franklin Reservoir, a chain of lakes that is not used for public drinking water, plus the Franklin State Forest, the Franklin Town Forests and the Ernest DelCarte Recreation and Conservation Area.

For a seller, wetlands and protected open space mean some lots carry limits on what can be built or cleared. If your house backs onto marsh, a brook or conservation land, ask the town before promising a buyer an addition or a new shed.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Franklin?
sections.html:
Franklin gets about 50 inches of precipitation and nearly 48 inches of snow in a normal year, based on NOAA 1991 to 2020 normals. Precipitation falls on about 125 days a year.

Snow load, ice and wet basements are the practical concerns. A buyer's inspector will look at the roof, gutters, sump pump and foundation, so a seller who has already addressed those items usually has fewer surprises during a sale.

sections.h2: How do people get around Franklin?
sections.html:
Franklin has two exits on Interstate 495, at Route 140 and King Street. The MBTA Franklin/Foxboro Line stops at Franklin and at Forge Park/495, and the town is in the GATRA service region, which offers demand-responsive transit.

  • Commuters value homes close to the Franklin or Forge Park stations.
  • Households that drive to jobs along I-495 value quick on-ramp access.
  • A short bike trail replaced the West Central Street bridge in 2017, and the Southern New England Trunkline Trail begins at Grove Street.

When you describe your property to a buyer, give the distance to a station or an I-495 exit. It answers a question almost every out-of-area buyer asks.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges are in Franklin?
sections.html:
Franklin Public Schools serves the town, and Franklin High School built a new building and demolished the old one in 2014. Tri-County Regional Vocational Technical High School accepts students from numerous nearby towns, and the Benjamin Franklin Classical Charter Public School serves kindergarten through eighth grade.

Dean College, founded in 1865, is a private residential college with over 1,100 students. It sits across the street from the library. Confirm school assignments with the district rather than relying on listing descriptions.

sections.h2: When are Franklin real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Franklin bills real estate and personal property tax quarterly, with due dates of August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. If a date lands on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

The Treasurer/Collector is at 355 East Central Street and can be reached at 508-520-4950. Payments by mail go to a lockbox in Boston, so check the town's page for the current address before mailing. You can pay online, at the drive-through window or in the office. The town also lets you request a municipal lien certificate online, and a buyer's attorney will normally order one before closing.

See the town's Treasurer/Collector page for payment options and the lien certificate form.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Norfolk County?
sections.html:
Franklin deeds are recorded at the Norfolk County Registry of Deeds, which charges an excise tax of $2.28 for each $500 of consideration, or fraction of that amount. The registry's own example shows that a $155,000 deed requires $706.80 in excise tax.

The recording fee for a deed is $156 for recorded land. The excise tax must be paid with an attorney's check or a bank check, separate from the recording fee check. Your closing attorney normally handles this, but it is worth knowing the figure so you can read your settlement statement. The registry publishes the schedule on its fee schedule page.

sections.h2: What does Franklin require for a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate?
sections.html:
Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 148, Section 26F and 26F 1/2 require the Fire Department to inspect a property for smoke and carbon monoxide alarm compliance when it is sold. In Franklin, inspections are held Monday through Friday from 9 am to 11 am, and you schedule through the town's online link or by calling 508-528-2323.

  • All smoke alarms must be photoelectric, or combination carbon monoxide and photoelectric. Ionization alarms are not allowed.
  • If a central station company such as ADT monitors the home, someone who can reset the system must be present.
  • Battery-operated Nest alarms are allowed only in homes built before 1975 that have not been substantially renovated.
  • Nest systems are not allowed in homes built or substantially renovated since 2008, which need heat detectors in garages.

The on-duty Battalion Chief does the inspection, so emergency calls can delay arrival. The town's scheduling page lists the details.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a Franklin house quickly?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell privately or accept a cash purchase. Listing works best when the house is clean and updated. A cash purchase suits owners who are dealing with an inherited house, a move that cannot wait or repairs they cannot afford.

Whichever route you choose, you will need the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate, a municipal lien certificate and a title that can be passed cleanly. Start those steps early so the closing date is not set by paperwork.

faqs.q: Is Franklin, MA a town or a city?
faqs.a: Franklin has a city form of government but keeps "Town of Franklin" as its official name. It is one of thirteen Massachusetts municipalities that did this.
Franklin is in Norfolk County, so deeds are recorded at the Norfolk County Registry of Deeds. Its published deeds excise tax is $2.28 per $500 of consideration.

faqs.q: When are Franklin property taxes due?
faqs.a: The due dates are August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. A date that falls on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Do ionization smoke alarms pass in Franklin?
faqs.a: No. Franklin's Fire Department requires photoelectric alarms, or combination carbon monoxide and photoelectric alarms, for home sale inspections.

faqs.q: How do I request a municipal lien certificate in Franklin?
faqs.a: The Treasurer/Collector's office handles it, and the town offers an online request along with a printable form. Your closing attorney usually asks for it before the sale.
